record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: In online graph coloring, vertices are presented one at a time in an externally determined order, and an online algorithm must irrevocably color each vertex using only the already revealed induced subgraph and its colors. For a graph G, chi_OL(G) is the smallest worst-case number of colors used by any online coloring algorithm over all vertex arrival orders. A graph class is online chi_OL-bounded if there is an online coloring algorithm A and a function h such that A uses at most h(chi_OL(G)) colors on every graph G in the class. Are chordal bipartite graphs online chi_OL-bounded?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the online graph coloring model, the vertices of a finite simple graph G are presented one at a time in an order chosen by an adversary. When a vertex v is presented, all edges between v and previously presented vertices are revealed, and an online algorithm must irrevocably assign v a color (a positive integer) such that adjacent vertices receive distinct colors; the algorithm has no knowledge of vertices that have not yet been presented. For an online algorithm A and a graph G, let A(G,σ) denote the number of colors A uses on G when vertices arrive in order σ. Define
  χ_OL(G) = min_A max_σ A(G,σ),
where the minimum is over all online coloring algorithms and the maximum is over all vertex arrival orders.

A class 𝒢 of graphs is said to be online χ_OL-bounded if there exists a single online coloring algorithm A and a function h : ℕ → ℕ such that for every G ∈ 𝒢 and every arrival order σ, A uses at most h(χ_OL(G)) colors on G.

A graph is chordal bipartite if it is bipartite and every induced cycle has length exactly 4 (equivalently, it contains no induced cycle of length at least 6 and no odd cycle).

Question: Is the class of chordal bipartite graphs online χ_OL-bounded?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of online χ_OL-boundedness for bipartite graphs (and its restricted subclasses) is described as a long-standing open question; partial positive results exist for P_k-free bipartite graphs for small k (e.g. P_8-free, even P_9-free), but no resolution for the full class of chordal bipartite graphs appears in the literature found. The status appears to be still open.

status_evidence.title: An On-line Competitive Algorithm for Coloring Bipartite Graphs Without Long Induced Paths
status_evidence.snippet: Partial positive results: classes of P_8-free bipartite and even P_9-free bipartite graphs are on-line χ_OL-bounded; general bipartite case remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Online χ_OL-boundedness is open for general bipartite graphs, with only partial results for forbidden induced path subclasses.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the question on online χ_OL-boundedness of chordal bipartite graphs as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem in a recent survey on graph coloring.
